title: Not Even a Hint: Guarding Your Heart Against Lust
author: Joshua Harris
edition_analyzed: Original 2003 edition (later republished as 'Sex Is Not the Problem — Lust Is')
target_audience: Individuals seeking to overcome struggles with lust
Anyone interested in biblical perspectives on sexual purity
core_themes: Pursuing sexual purity in a hypersexualized culture
Identifying and resisting lustful thoughts and behaviors
Applying biblical teachings to modern temptations
Practical strategies for guarding one's heart and mind
primary_purpose: To provide frank, practical, and biblically-grounded guidance to help Christians recognize, resist, and overcome lust in thought and behavior, cultivating purity in a culture where temptations are pervasive.

structure_format.organization: Divided into topical chapters, each addressing different aspects of lust and purity
features: Personal stories and confessions from the author

key_concepts_lessons: Lust is a heart issue, not just a behavior problem.
God calls believers to a radical standard: not even a hint of sexual immorality.
A 'don't ask, don't tell' approach to sin is harmful; honest confession and accountability are vital.
Practical disciplines—including thought life management, media choices, and community—help build defenses against lust.
God’s grace offers hope and empowers lasting change, even when repeated failure occurs.
True purity flows from loving God and embracing his vision for sexuality, not mere rule-following.
notable_features: Open acknowledgment of sexual struggle among Christians
Balanced approach—neither demonizing sexuality nor excusing lust
Questions for self-reflection and group discussion
cultural_historical_context: Published at a time when church conversations about sexuality were often either legalistic or avoided, the book offered a candid, grace-filled approach to sexual purity for young Christians navigating the influences of early internet culture and shifting sexual norms.
reception_impact: Well-received for its honesty and practical approach among Christian readers
Used widely in accountability groups, youth ministries, and church studies
Some readers found the approach refreshingly grace-centered; others saw it as too conservative or rooted in purity culture debates
Later editions addressed feedback and included updated language
comparable_titles: Every Man’s Battle by Stephen Arterburn and Fred Stoeker
Sex Is Not the Problem (Lust Is) by Joshua Harris (the book’s retitled edition)
When God Writes Your Love Story by Eric and Leslie Ludy
